title: The Tally of Dishonor
issueFunction: Financial legibility as a modern form of status and participation. Bjorn must become recognizable to a bank without surrendering his own understanding of value; Carrie translates the household into acceptable documents; Gunnar contributes practical pattern-reading; the toaster becomes a tangible sign that the group has gained partial civic agency.
causalSpine: The provisional-status deadline forces the bank trip.
Identity, address, value, and access become procedural gates.
Carrie translates DTI reality into ordinary bank requirements and exceptions.
Gunnar's observation of routes, transactions, and institutional behavior materially helps the group progress.
Bjorn responds most strongly to tangible value, obligation, and revocable authority.
The promotional toaster resolves the issue's argument about tangible value and status.
Completed paperwork leaves the Vikings more administratively legible and less dependent.

issueCharacterState.Bjorn: Sovereignty and provision drive his objections to intangible or revocable forms of value.
issueCharacterState.Carrie: Her procedural competence drives the institutional victory.
issueCharacterState.Gunnar: Issue 3 competence carries forward into useful observation of financial space and procedure.
issueCharacterState.bankStaff: Ordinary employees working rationally inside a system designed for contemporary customers.

continuity: The Bushwick apartment is already established home and proof-of-address friction arises because paperwork lags lived reality.
DTI documents are ordinary municipal paperwork.
The bank is an ordinary 2026 commercial environment.
Legacy S1E02 payload IDs remain stable production identifiers for this Issue 4 material.
readerOutcome: The reader should understand why the account matters now, what blocks it, what Carrie changes, what Gunnar contributes, why Bjorn resists the bank's abstractions, why the toaster matters, and what concrete capability the household gains.
